profile_md: Paris-Saclay pages do not show a university-wide student-project scheme; employer-linked work is distributed across components. The strongest verified routes are at CentraleSupélec (a member institution): Projet SIC (3CV2500, Jean Muller projects), where teams of 3-4 work on a problem proposed by an industrial, institutional or associative 'client' who receives interim and final deliverables (2025-2026, ~240 h), and Projet S8 (groups of 5, client unnamed, C unclear). In the Faculté des Sciences d'Orsay, the GenAI26 hackathon (March 2026, 7 days, ~150 students from six AI/data programmes) had teams building prototypes for challenges set by IBM, Mastercard and SNCF Réseau. A 3-day consulting module in an M2 management/communication master involves client briefs but is described as simulated. Polytech, IUT d'Orsay, pharmacy hackathon and the legal clinic are leads without verified group/client evidence. Source pages are French; extracts translated. Uncertain: compulsory status, credits, partner coverage, and whether CentraleSupélec counts within the University perimeter.
gaps: Further departmental capstones (Polytech, IUT SAÉ, other master projets tutorés) likely exist; IAE Paris-Saclay/Faculté Jean Monnet, medicine and Polytech not researched in depth (reduced-depth mode). Starthèse legacy row not re-fetched. Retrieval via WebFetch summaries (small-model paraphrase of French pages), not direct verbatim page text.
